meridian_skill.description:
Skill validation framework PLUS daily test-suite health and regression
intelligence. Validates skill conformance (frontmatter, manifest coverage,
resolver coverage). Runs the project test suite in tiered phases (unit /
evals / integration / system health), classifies failures, and produces
a regression-aware report.
meridian_skill.name: testing

sections.heading: Two modes
lines: This skill has two related but distinct modes:
**Skill conformance validation** — gbrain's own conformance bar
(the original 1.0 scope). Validates every skill has SKILL.md with
frontmatter, every reference exists, manifest + resolver coverage
round-trips
**Project test-suite health (v0.25.1 extension)** — runs the
project's tiered test suite and produces a regression-classified
report. Used by daily cron, container-restart bootstrap, and
"how are the tests" prompts
Pick the mode by trigger

sections.heading: Contract
lines: `skills/manifest.json` lists every skill directory
`skills/RESOLVER.md` references every skill in the manifest
`openclaw.plugin.json` `skills[]` round-trips with both
No MECE violations (duplicate triggers across skills)

sections.heading: Contract — steps
lines: Every skill directory has a `SKILL.md` file
Every `SKILL.md` has valid YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`)
Every `SKILL.md` has required sections per
`test/skills-conformance.test.ts`

sections.heading: Phases
lines: Walk skills directory. List all subdirs containing `SKILL.md`
Parse YAML, check required fields
Check for the required headings
Check manifest. Every skill dir must be in `manifest.json`
Every manifest skill must have a RESOLVER row
RESOLVER trigger ↔ frontmatter triggers
Report results

sections.heading: Daily run protocol
lines: When the cron fires (or the user asks), do ALL of this:
Parse: total passed, total failed, total skipped, file-level results
codeblock:bash:YnVuIHRlc3QgMj4mMQ==
Parse: same format. Note any flakes (tests that fail due to API
timeouts, not code bugs)
codeblock:bash:IyBBZGFwdCB0byB0aGUgcHJvamVjdCdzIGV2YWwgY29uZmlnCmJ1biB0ZXN0IC0tZmlsdGVyIGV2YWwgMj4mMQ==
Disk / memory / CPU
gbrain: `gbrain doctor --fast --json`
Database connection (if applicable)
Critical files exist (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, etc.)
Check if the test itself was modified recently (test change, not
regression)
Check if the code it tests was modified recently (possible
regression)
Check if it's a known flake (API timeout, service down)
Check if a dependency was updated (gbrain, bun, etc.)
codeblock:bash:IyBXaGF0IGNoYW5nZWQgc2luY2UgbGFzdCB0ZXN0IHJ1bj8KZ2l0IGxvZyAtLW9uZWxpbmUgLS1zaW5jZT0iMjQgaG91cnMgYWdvIg==
For each failing test:

table:decision:

codeblock:plain:
**DO auto-fix:**
Test expects an old file path after a rename → update the test
Test expects an old version string → update
Test expects a file that was intentionally deleted → remove the test
Import path broke because file moved → fix the import
**DO NOT auto-fix:**
Test expects behavior A but code now does B → ASK first. Maybe the
test is right and the code has a bug
When uncertain: check the commit message that changed the code, check
if there's a related PR or conversation, ask the user if still unclear
Security test failing → ALWAYS escalate, never auto-fix
use judgment to follow the 7. Auto-fix protocol — steps 2 guidance:
Test was skipped with a TODO → don't un-skip without understanding why

sections.heading: Anti-Patterns
lines: ❌ Skipping conformance validation after adding a new skill
❌ Adding skills to `manifest.json` without adding to RESOLVER.md
❌ Treating every red test as a regression. Classify first; many are
stale or flaky
❌ Auto-"fixing" a security test failure
❌ Reporting "all clear" without actually running system health checks

sections.heading: Anti-Patterns — steps
lines: use judgment to follow the Anti-Patterns — steps guidance:
❌ Auto-un-skipping a test without understanding why it was skipped

sections.heading: Contract
lines: This skill guarantees:

Output written under the directories listed in `writes_to:` (when applicable)
Conventions referenced (`quality.md`, `brain-first.md`, `_brain-filing-rules.md`) are followed
Privacy contract preserved: no real names, no fork-specific filesystem path literals, no upstream-fork references
The full behavior contract is documented in the body sections above; this section exists for the conformance test

prose_steps.text:
Decide which case below applies and carry out its action:
- when Tier is Unit, What it runs is `bun test` (deterministic, zero external calls), Wall time is <2s, Every commit
- when Tier is Evals, What it runs is LLM-judge or quality evals, Wall time is ~60s, Daily
- when Tier is Integration, What it runs is E2E tests against real Postgres, Wall time is ~5m, Pre-ship + nightly
- when Tier is System health, What it runs is Disk / memory / CPU / service liveness, Wall time is <10s, Daily
